chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAbdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام): “I mix with the people, and I often find myself amazed at some people who do not hold your wilayah and instead follow so-and-so and so-and-so, yet they possess trustworthiness, truthfulness, and loyalty; and there are other people who hold your wilayah, but they do not possess that trustworthiness, loyalty, or truthfulness.”

He said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh (عليه السلام) sat upright and turned toward me as one angered, then said: “There is no religion for one who worships Allah through the wilayah of a tyrannical Imam who is not from Allah, and there is no blame upon one who follows the wilayah of a just Imam from Allah.”
I said: “There is no religion for those, and there is no blame upon these?” He said: “Yes, there is no religion for those, and there is no blame upon these.”
Then he said: “Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ‘Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light’?”
It means: from the darknesses of sins to the light of tawbah and forgiveness, because of their wilayah toward every just Imam from Allah.
And He said: ‘As for those who disbelieve, their guardians are the ṭāghūt; they bring them out of the light into the darknesses.’

What is meant by this is that they had been upon the light of Islam; then when they took the wilayah of every tyrannical Imam who was not from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, they departed by that allegiance to him from the light of Islam into the darknesses of disbelief. So Allah made the Fire incumbent upon them along with the disbelievers: ‘Those are the companions of the Fire; they shall remain therein forever.’

key_terms.إِمَامٍ جَائِرٍ: a tyrannical Imam or illegitimate leader who is not appointed by Allah
key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ: a just Imam appointed by Allah
key_terms.التَّوْبَةِ: tawbah; repentance by which one returns from sin
key_terms.الطَّاغُوتُ: false or tyrannical authority that leads people away from divine guidance
key_terms.الظُّلُمَاتِ: the darknesses; interpreted here as sins and, later, disbelief
key_terms.النُّورِ: the light; interpreted here as tawbah, forgiveness, and the light of Islam
key_terms.وَلَايَةِ: wilayah; divinely significant allegiance and authority, here referring to allegiance to the rightful Imam

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) explain the role of wilayah in faith and Qur'an 2:257?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true religion is inseparable from the wilayah of the just Imam appointed by Allah, and that outward moral traits alone do not substitute for correct religious allegiance. It also interprets Qur'an 2:257 through the lens of wilayah, describing just Imamic authority as a means of being brought from darkness into light, and tyrannical authority as a cause of falling from the light of Islam into the darkness of disbelief.
